headline: It’s all about the machines
dek: Six days after the midterm elections, the President questions whether the vote was honest, asks how the polls could be so wrong, and blames early-voting “dumps” and voting machines. He offers no evidence in the post.

original.speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Does anybody really believe that this “Election” was honest. How could the Polls be so wrong??? Some early voting “dumps” were so large that it was impossible to win, no matter how many people went to  vote.
It’s all about the machines, which are far more important than the voter! President DJT
original.context: Posted on 9 November 2026, six days after the US midterm elections of 3 November.

verification.note: Copied by the editor from truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump on 9 November 2026 (shown as Nov 09, 2026, 7:07 AM Pacific). The double space before “vote” is in the post.

en: I share the frustration of many Americans who hoped for a different result, and who were surprised by how far the polls were from the outcome.

Where there are concerns about early voting or voting machines, they should be examined by election officials and, if necessary, by the courts, on the evidence. Confidence in our elections matters more than any single result.
fr: Je partage la déception de nombreux Américains qui espéraient un autre résultat, et qui ont été surpris de voir à quel point les sondages s’en écartaient.

Là où le vote anticipé ou les machines de vote suscitent des inquiétudes, elles doivent être examinées par les responsables électoraux et, si nécessaire, par les tribunaux, sur la base de preuves. La confiance dans nos élections compte davantage que n’importe quel résultat.

neuchatelois.hook: Trois cents pièces, toutes à leur place. On va *ouvrir le boîtier.*
neuchatelois.hookEn: Three hundred parts, all in place. Let’s *open the case.*
text: Est-ce que quelqu’un croit vraiment que cette « élection » était honnête ? Comment les sondages ont-ils pu se tromper à ce point ? Il paraît que certains « paquets » de votes anticipés étaient si gros qu’on ne pouvait pas gagner.

Moi, je vous le dis : tout est dans la machine. Chez nous, une machine, on la démonte, on regarde chaque pièce à la loupe, et on la remonte. Trois cents pièces, toutes à leur place. Alors on va ouvrir le boîtier. Et si tout tourne rond… bon, on dira que c’est le sondage qui retardait.
en: Does anybody really believe that this “election” was honest? How could the polls be so wrong? Apparently some “bundles” of early votes were so big you couldn’t win.

I’m telling you: it’s all in the machine. Round here, a machine, you take it apart, you check every piece under the magnifying glass, and you put it back together. Three hundred parts, all in place. So we’ll open the case. And if everything runs like clockwork… well, we’ll say it was the poll that was running slow.
notes: Neuchâtel and its Jura mountains are the heart of Swiss watchmaking, where a fine mechanical watch can count several hundred parts.

genevois.hook: On crée une commission. *Dans dix ans, on saura.*
genevois.hookEn: We set up a commission. *In ten years, we’ll know.*
text: Quelqu’un croit vraiment que cette « élection » était honnête ? Les sondages, se tromper à ce point ? Et ces « paquets » de votes anticipés, si gros qu’on ne pouvait pas gagner, paraît-il.

Remarquez, à Genève, on a une commission pour tout. Je propose qu’on en crée une pour les machines : elle se réunira au bord du lac, elle demandera un rapport, puis un deuxième rapport. Dans dix ans, on saura. Et si les machines sont innocentes, on dira que c’était les sondages.
en: Does anybody really believe this “election” was honest? The polls, that wrong? And those “bundles” of early votes, so big you couldn’t win, apparently.

Mind you, in Geneva we have a commission for everything. I suggest we set one up for the machines: it’ll meet by the lake, ask for a report, then a second report. In ten years, we’ll know. And if the machines turn out to be innocent, we’ll say it was the polls.
notes: Geneva, home to the United Nations’ European headquarters and dozens of international organisations, is famous for its commissions, working groups and very long reports.

breton.hook: Quand le bateau ne rentre pas, *on ne dit pas que la mer a triché.*
breton.hookEn: When the boat doesn’t come home, *you don’t say the sea cheated.*
text: Vous croyez vraiment que cette « élection » était honnête ? Les sondages, se tromper autant ? Et ces « paquets » de votes anticipés, tellement gros qu’on ne pouvait pas gagner, à ce qu’on m’a dit.
C’est les machines, voilà tout. Chez nous, quand le bateau ne rentre pas, on ne dit pas que la mer a triché. On regarde la météo, le moteur, et le capitaine. Bon. Je commencerai par le moteur.
en: Do you really believe this “election” was honest? The polls, that far off? And those “bundles” of early votes, so big you couldn’t win, or so I was told.
It’s the machines, that’s all. Round here, when the boat doesn’t come home, you don’t say the sea cheated. You look at the weather, the engine, and the captain. Right. I’ll start with the engine.
notes: Brittany, France’s great fishing region, has a long tradition of quiet stubbornness in the face of the sea and the weather.

chti.hook: On recompte *tant qu’il reste des gaufres.*
chti.hookEn: We recount *as long as there are waffles left.*
text: Qui c’est qui croit vraiment que cette « élection », elle était honnête ? Les sondages, ils se sont trompés comme ça ? Et ces « tas » de votes anticipés, si gros qu’on pouvait pas gagner, à ce qu’y paraît.

Tout cha, ch’est les machines. Chez nous, on dépouille à la main, à la salle des fêtes, avec du café et des gaufres, et on recompte tant qu’il reste des gaufres. Alors envoyez-moi les bulletins, j’apporte les gaufres. Le résultat, on verra demain.
en: Who really believes this “election” was honest? The polls got it that wrong? And those “piles” of early votes, so big you couldn’t win, so they say.

It’s all the machines. Round here, we count the ballots by hand in the village hall, with coffee and waffles, and we recount as long as there are waffles left. So send me the ballots, I’ll bring the waffles. We’ll see about the result tomorrow.
notes: In France, ballots are counted by hand in most polling stations, in public, by volunteers. Filled waffles (gaufres fourrées) are a speciality of Lille; “tout cha, ch’est” is “all that, it’s” in Picard.

california.hook: Every machine has a bug. *Usually it’s the user.*
text: Does anyone honestly believe that “election” was legit? Like, how were the polls that off? I’m hearing some early-vote “drops” were so huge you literally couldn’t win.
It’s all about the machines, honestly. I asked a friend in Palo Alto, and he said every machine has a bug, and the bug is usually the user. I’m choosing not to take that personally.
en: He doubts the election was fair, wonders how the polls missed so badly, and says, without evidence, that some batches of early votes were too big to beat.
He blames the machines, but a tech friend from Silicon Valley tells him the usual problem with any machine is the person using it. He decides not to hear it.

midwest.hook: Gary counts everything twice. *That’s suspicious too.*
text: Well, I don’t want to make a fuss, but does anybody really think that “election” was on the up-and-up? Those polls sure missed by a country mile. And I hear some of those early-vote “dumps” were awful big.

Now, I’m no expert, but I figure it’s the machines. Back home we’d just ask Gary at the county clerk’s office to take a look. Gary counts everything twice. Gary has never once found a problem, which, honestly, is a little suspicious too.
en: Very politely, he wonders whether the election was honest (“on the up-and-up”), notes the polls were far off (“by a country mile”) and repeats what he has heard about large batches of early votes.
He blames the machines, and suggests asking a careful local election clerk, whose failure to ever find anything wrong he now finds suspicious.

london.hook: It wasn’t me. *It was signal failure at Baker Street.*
text: Does anyone seriously believe that “election” was honest? How could the polls be that wrong? Apparently, some of the early-vote “dumps” were so big you simply couldn’t win.
It’s all about the machines, which matter far more than the voters. In London we have a name for that: the Tube defence. It wasn’t me, it was a signal failure at Baker Street.
en: He questions whether the election was honest, asks how the polls got it so wrong, and repeats a claim about huge batches of early votes.
Blaming the machines rather than the voters is, to a Londoner, like blaming a late arrival on the Underground’s famous “signal failure”: always possible, never quite convincing.

text: His Majesty’s Government has every confidence in the ability of the United States to count its own votes, as it has done, with occasional excitement, for the best part of two and a half centuries.
We would note that polls are opinions, whereas ballots are counted. The distinction has served us both well.
en: He did not like the result.
He would rather blame the machines than the voters, who will, after all, be voting again.

text: France has full confidence in American democracy, and in the officials and volunteers who count the votes in every county.
In France, most ballots are still counted by hand, in public, in schools and town halls, and any citizen may watch. It is slow, a little old-fashioned, and very hard to argue with.
fr: La France a pleine confiance dans la démocratie américaine, ainsi que dans les responsables et les bénévoles qui comptent les voix dans chaque comté.

En France, la plupart des bulletins sont encore dépouillés à la main, en public, dans les écoles et les mairies, et tout citoyen peut y assister. C’est lent, un peu désuet, et très difficile à contester.
notes: In France, the count (le dépouillement) is public: any voter may attend, and volunteers from among the voters do the counting.

text: The Federal Council takes note of the President’s concerns.

In Switzerland, most citizens vote by post, several weeks in advance. The envelopes arrive in the communes in great numbers; we have never thought of calling them dumps. The results are counted and published commune by commune, and the people accept them, sometimes grumbling, which is also a Swiss tradition.
fr: Le Conseil fédéral prend acte des préoccupations du Président.

En Suisse, la plupart des citoyens votent par correspondance, plusieurs semaines à l’avance. Les enveloppes arrivent en grand nombre dans les communes ; il ne nous est jamais venu à l’idée de parler de « déversements ». Les résultats sont dépouillés et publiés commune par commune, et le peuple les accepte, parfois en râlant, ce qui est aussi une tradition suisse.
notes: Most Swiss voters vote by post: the material arrives at home three to four weeks before the vote.
